_readme: Reviewed, dated exceptions to the release-tooling supply-chain gate
(scripts/release-tooling-audit.sh, Verjson/.github#146). Every entry excuses
exactly one advisory and EXPIRES on its review-by date: past that, CI fails
again until a human re-assesses or upstream ships a fix. An entry that stops
matching a reported advisory also fails, so a resolved exception cannot linger
as dead permission. Adding an entry means accepting a known risk — say why, and
keep the window short.
Fields, all required and all enforced: ghsa (GHSA id), package and severity —
which must match the advisory exactly as npm reports it, so an entry excuses
that one advisory and no other — reason, and review-by (YYYY-MM-DD, a real
calendar date no more than 90 days out).
severity is COPIED from the advisory as npm reports it (case-insensitively),
never chosen as a risk level. Rounding one up 'to be safe' does not make a
stricter exception — it matches no reported advisory, and the gate rejects it
as dead permission.
Scope, precisely: an entry excuses an ADVISORY, not a package. npm propagates
one advisory outward along `via`, so a single entry clears every high/critical
package whose chain resolves ONLY to advisories it excuses — often more than
the package it names. It never clears a package npm grades ABOVE the entry's
severity, and never one whose chain also reaches an advisory nobody excused.

allowlist.reason: DoS via unbounded expansion in the copy of brace-expansion bundled inside npm's own CLI (semantic-release -> @semantic-release/npm -> npm), reached only when semantic-release publishes on our own runners against our own inputs — not attacker-reachable in CI. No upstream fix is installable as of 2026-07-25: npm bundles the dependency, so `overrides` cannot rewrite it, and no npm release yet carries brace-expansion 5.0.8.
